crime: Whenever {WITCH_NAME} asked if she could stay, her foster mother went to the hall telephone, dialed every digit of the agency's number except the last, and rested a finger in that final hole.

In the mansion, one girl sat on the upper railing every evening, legs dangling over the courtyard. It was the only place inside, she said, that felt like outside. {WITCH_NAME} stood on the floor beside her, held the hem of the girl's skirt and asked, "Can I hold on tomorrow?" The answer was always "Keep holding on."

One day at the fountain, the girl told a friend, "If {WITCH_NAME} asks one more time whether she can hold on, I'm climbing onto that railing without her." In her cell, {WITCH_NAME} heard every word as if the girl sat beside her, her own name in the middle. The girl said nothing more.
During evening free time, {WITCH_NAME} took the girl's hem without asking. Then she let go and pushed her over.
The prisoners heard the fall and found the girl on the rim of the fountain. They phoned the three girls at the lake at once.

{WITCH_NAME} had told no one what her Magic did, so the prisoners said her name freely. In the trial court, she said she had followed the three on their evening walk to the lake and sat under the trees ten paces behind. She recited every line they had said about her until the phone rang. The last was "She'd never really climb onto that railing without {WITCH_NAME}." The girls confirmed every word, and that line had come after the fall. The prisoners ruled her out.
Then the friend from the fountain spoke up. She had whispered that last line behind her hand, into one girl's ear. The third girl, right beside them, never heard it.
The prisoners understood. She had never gone to the lake; her Magic had carried every line to her while she stood at the railing.
fields.epitaph: Every sentence with her name in it reached her; the answer she needed never said her name.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Asks If She May Stay
execution: A giant hall telephone rose, and she was strapped on her back in its cradle, her head under the mouthpiece end. The dial turned through its last digit, and the bell rang. The handset came down onto the cradle. Its mouthpiece cup closed over her head and sealed at her shoulders. Inside, she asked into the mouthpiece, "Can I stay?" Muffled, the question came again, fainter, then stopped. The handset rested on its cradle. The bell was silent, and nothing stirred beneath.

magic.name: Near as a Whisper
magic.text: She can clearly hear anyone who says her name, from any distance.
